title: A linear rational coordinate with transcendental residue
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed field [def-kun-separably-closed] and let $K(t)$ be the fraction field of the polynomial ring $K[t]$ in one indeterminate [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-pc-field-extension]. Let $O\subseteq K(t)$ be a valuation subring, let $R=O\cap K$, and assume $\operatorname{trdeg}_{\kappa(R)}\kappa(O)=1$ [def-kun-transcendence-degree]. Then there exist $a\in K$ and $\pi\in K^\times$ such that $z=(t-a)/\pi\in O^\times$ and the residue $\bar z\in\kappa(O)$ is transcendental over $\kappa(R)$ (no nonzero polynomial over $\kappa(R)$ vanishes on it). If $t\in O$ and the prime $\mathfrak m_O\cap R[t]$ is maximal and contracts to $\mathfrak m_R$, these choices can be made with $a\in R$ and $0\ne\pi\in\mathfrak m_R$. Here a valuation subring $B$ of a field $F$ [def-weil-field] means a subring with fraction field $F$ such that, for every $z\in F^\times$, $z\in B$ or $z^{-1}\in B$. Its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_B=B\setminus B^\times$ and its residue field is $\kappa(B)=B/\mathfrak m_B$ [def-weil-residue-field].
